This suggests that your earlier academic record showed some potential, but it was not enough to offset the strong negative signals from your class ranks. To improve your chances, focus on strengthening the areas within your control. Retake the LSAT after thorough preparation, and consider enrolling in rigorous academic or bar-preparatory courses. If possible, complete additional coursework or a post-baccalaureate program to raise your grades and demonstrate sustained academic improvement. Reapplying with a stronger record and a higher LSAT score could change this prediction.
